new_statements.quote: III. Intonation und Akzent. Die Sprache hat semantische Tonhöhen, vgl. n̥' „ich" und n̥, neben hn „sie", tu'? „wer?" und tu „hören". Die gepreßten Vokale, siehe oben unter I, scheinen Tiefton zu haben, aber es gibt tieftonige Vokale, die nicht gepreßt sind. Zuweilen ist der dynamische Akzent von mir durch einen Akut bezeichnet.
new_statements.translation: III. Intonation and accent. The language has semantic pitch levels (tone heights), cf. n̥' 'I' and n̥, beside hn 'they/she', tu'? 'who?' and tu 'to hear'. The pressed vowels, see above under I, seem to have low tone, but there are low-toned vowels that are not pressed. Occasionally the dynamic accent has been marked by me with an acute.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The language is tonal (lexically contrastive pitch levels, incl. a low tone associated with pressed vowels); a dynamic (stress) accent also exists but Meinhof only occasionally marks it with an acute and gives no rule for where it falls — no fixed or predictable word-stress position is stated.
new_statements.exceptions: Pressed (pharyngealised) vowels seem to take low tone, but there are low-toned vowels that are not pressed; the acute for dynamic accent is used only 'zuweilen' (occasionally), so no exhaustive marking.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: the tone minimal pairs are monosyllabic words/pronouns (n̥' 'ich' vs n̥, hn 'sie'; tu'? 'wer?' vs tu 'hören'); 'dynamischer Akzent' marked with an acute on individual words in the sketch and vocabulary, never assigned by rule. Elicited from one elderly speaker (Kunraad Stazen, c. 60, Warrenton/Pniel).
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog's 'Danster !Ui' [dans1240] (alt. name ǁKx'au) is Güldemann's (2019) cover term for two Vaal-River !Ui doculects: ǂUngkue [kxau1242] = the variety Meinhof recorded in 1928 from Kunraad Stazen (c. 60 y.) of the Warrenton/Pniel mission communities near Kimberley (Bleek 1956 labels it SIIb 'ǁkxau, near Kimberley'), and ǁKã [kaaa1239] recorded by D. F. Bleek. The statement quoted therefore describes ǂUngkue/ǁKx'au specifically, not ǁKã; 'Danster' itself is a 19th-century San man (photographed 1863-66, Bainsvlei/Quaggafontein, Orange Free State) after whom Güldemann named the unit, and no Danster wordlist was examined.
